solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cut off brewer's cart reversing in naval establishment

parts.note: to dock is to cut off, as with a tail

indicators.note: says the cart's word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a dray is the low flat cart brewers used for barrels

explanation.surface: A brewery cart backs into a navy base and loses something on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A dray is the heavy horse-drawn cart brewers used to deliver barrels; 'Cut off' is a verb here, as in docking a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dockyard is the yard where navy ships are built and repaired, a naval facility.

clue.text: Tranquillising drug, one taken with hesitation after work

indicators.note: places the first two pieces following the word for work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral one
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone pauses before taking a sedative after a day's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium, from poppies, is a narcotic that sedates and calms.

clue.text: Fellow clan member finally seen in mask, surprisingly

indicators.note: signals that the gathered letters come out in an unexpected new order
asks for only the closing letter of the word seen

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A tribesman is unexpectedly spotted wearing a mask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is anagram fodder rather than a link word: IN and MASK are rearranged, and 'finally' adds the closing letter of 'seen' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a male relative, and clans are groups bound by kinship.

clue.text: It sounds like everything a cobbler needs

indicators.note: tells us the word for everything is spoken and we write a different spelling

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A shoemaker claims he needs everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'a cobbler needs', meaning something a cobbler needs.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is the pointed tool shoemakers use to pierce leather for stitching.

clue.text: Refusing to be going downhill

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... an offer means refusing it

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests refusing to ski or walk down a hill; really it is two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both turning something down politely and deteriorating or sloping downward.

clue.text: A function originally held in church eating-place

indicators.note: puts the first pieces within the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: asks for the opening letter of function

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A social function is held in a church that doubles as a place to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a small restaurant serving light meals and drinks.

clue.text: A great ape caught him up at last

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: asks for only the final letter of up

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: An ape finally catches up with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimpanzee is one of the great apes, alongside gorillas and orangutans.

clue.text: Prospective groom accepting new money

indicators.note: the groom's word takes in the letter for new, holding it within

parts.note: a fiance is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A husband-to-be accepts fresh money, perhaps a dowry.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means funds or money resources, as in arranging finance for a purchase.

clue.text: Gesture of great importance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sign or motion conveying a message
second meaning: ... as an adjective, notable or striking, as in a ... victory

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective sense, as in 'a signal honour', is less familiar than the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a communicating motion and an adjective for something outstanding.

clue.text: Customer's legal right protected by court

indicators.note: the court letters surround and shield the right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A shopper's statutory rights are upheld by a court.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services from a professional, a patron.

clue.text: Spiritual leader, one with mother in Newcastle?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mam is the northern English (Geordie) word for mum

explanation.surface: A religious leader lives with his mother in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle is in north-east England, where mother is commonly 'mam'; the question mark flags the regional usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and is a Muslim religious leader.

clue.text: Frivolous old man after power in N Wales town

indicators.note: puts the combined letters inside the town's name

parts.note: Flint is a town in north Wales

indicators.note: places the word for old man following the letter for power

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A frivolous old man trails behind someone powerful in a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means lacking proper seriousness, treating matters lightly.

clue.text: Abandoned infant worrying don in gulf

indicators.note: worrying something can mean tugging it about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A university don frets about a gulf, or an infant left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the anagram fodder, not a link word: DON + IN + GULF rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is a baby found after being deserted by unknown parents.

clue.text: Indian peasant at entrance to university

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer or peasant

indicators.note: asks for the opening letter of university

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A farmworker from India stands at the gates of a university.
explanation.walkthrough: HIND as a rustic farm worker is old-fashioned, not the female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu follows Hinduism, the chief religion of India, so can be called Indian.

clue.text: Searched around area regularly visited by ghosts

indicators.note: the word for searched goes round the letter for area

parts.note: hunted means searched

explanation.surface: Someone combed a district often frequented by spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunted house is one where ghosts are said to appear repeatedly.

clue.text: Fireplace in entertaining legend

indicators.note: says the letters are found within the next two words, running across them

explanation.surface: A legend is told around a hearth to entertain listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a domestic hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Old astronomer's girl and boy touring island

indicators.note: the girl and boy go around the letter for island

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
Leo is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A couple travel round an island with an astronomer's telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei, the 17th-century Italian scientist, pioneered telescopic observation of the heavens.

clue.text: Good Scottish party welcomed by eg assistance animal

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good

indicators.note: the letters EG take the party word inside them

parts.note: taken as written
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A good Scottish party greets, say, an assistance dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg' looks like 'for example' but supplies its own two letters, which wrap around DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide dog is trained to lead a blind or partially sighted person.

clue.text: Represented on paper as tired and haggard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sketched, made into a picture
second meaning: looking strained and exhausted

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: a past participle of sketching, and an adjective for a worn face.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pictured with pencil and looking gaunt from fatigue or worry.

clue.text: Cover over, at first, open-air swimming pool

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: asks for only the opening letter of over

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone first pulls a cover over an outdoor pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public outdoor pool, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Doctor with a degree in theatre studies

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A doctor holds a degree in theatre studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama is the academic subject of plays and performance, studied at school and university.

clue.text: Sheets of cloud included in illustration

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the word illustration

explanation.surface: A picture shows layers of cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Strati, plural of stratus, are low flat grey cloud layers.

clue.text: Post tablet a doctor finally supplies

parts.note: a pill is a tablet

indicators.note: asks for only the closing letter of doctor

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: A doctor ends up prescribing a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright post supporting a structure.

clue.text: Drink brought up for friend

indicators.note: in a down clue this reads the word for drink from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A drink is fetched for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Pal is informal for a companion or mate.

clue.text: Old PM without teeth leaving gallery

indicators.note: the gallery's name departs from the word for toothless

parts.note: edentate means toothless
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: An elderly prime minister leaves a gallery having lost his teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without teeth' is not a deletion of letters here but the word EDENTATE; take TATE from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: In Irish county, see Scottish cow, perhaps

indicators.note: places the word for see inside the county's name

parts.note: Galway is a county in the west of Ireland
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Someone in an Irish county spots a cow from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloway is a hardy black beef cattle breed from south-west Scotland; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
